proposal: The Mandate recommends making Medicaid program integrity a state responsibility with incentives: an enhanced contingency fee for states that cut waste and fraud, the 90/10 IT match for fraud and eligibility systems, and positive-return programs without waivers. status_summary: Public Law 119-21, approved 2025-07-04, added Medicaid provisions that align with parts of this recommendation: address verification from 2027-01-01 and a federal duplicate-enrollment check from 2029-10-01 (section 71103), quarterly death file checks for enrollees from 2027-01-01 and for providers from 2028-01-01 (sections 71104 and 71105), a requirement from fiscal year 2030 that the Secretary issue eligibility-related disallowances for state error rates above 3 percent, with the Secretary's good-faith waiver authority restricted (section 71106), six-month redeterminations for the expansion adult group from 2027-01-01 (section 71107) and a $1 million home equity cap for long-term care eligibility from 2028-01-01 (section 71108). These are enacted and have drawn CMS guidance (an informational bulletin of 2025-11-18 and a State Medicaid Director Letter of 2026-03-06), but none is operative before 2027-01-01. No enhanced contingency fee, expanded 90/10 match for fraud systems or waiver-free positive-return programs was found, and the managed care provisions found are limited to a duty for plans to send address data to states (section 71103) and a bar on plans determining community engagement compliance (section 71119). Separately, HHS announced on 2025-07-17 a CMS review of duplicate Medicaid and CHIP enrollment across states and Exchanges, with state lists for eligibility rechecks; this administrative step predates and is distinct from the enacted statutory checks.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was approved. Its Medicaid chapter includes sections 71103 (duplicate enrollment and address verification), 71104 and 71105 (deceased enrollees and providers), 71106 (payment reduction for certain erroneous excess payments), 71107 (eligibility redeterminations) and 71108 (home equity limit).

HHS announced that CMS identified about 2.8 million people enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP in more than one state or in both Medicaid/CHIP and a subsidized Exchange plan, and that CMS would give states lists to recheck eligibility.

CMS posted an overview slide deck on implementing section 71107 (eligibility redeterminations), summarizing State Medicaid Director Letter #26-001, on its guidance page for the 2025 reconciliation law.

title: Medicaid program integrity: contingency fees, improper eligibility penalties, asset tests
uncertainties: Mandate text on page 467 was checked. Sections 71103 to 71106 were read in the CMS informational bulletin of 2025-11-18 and sections 71103 to 71108 in the CMS legislation overview slide on the medicaid.gov host; section 71107 was read in State Medicaid Director Letter #26-001. The GovInfo body text of Public Law 119-21 is truncated before Subtitle B, so the statutory text, including the $1 million home equity amount (taken from the MACPAC September 2025 summary), was not read. The CMS bulletin states that the 3 percent error-rate threshold existed in prior law and that section 71106 restricts rather than removes the Secretary's waiver authority. No enhanced contingency fee or 90/10 match for fraud systems appears in the CMS summaries; this is an absence in summaries, not a check of the statute. A Federal Register API search of CMS documents published since 2026-04-01 (run 2026-11-03) returned a proposed rule on indirect hold harmless thresholds, the CY 2027 physician fee schedule proposed rule, an information collection notice and the community engagement rule (Doc. 2026-11094), none of which implements sections 71103 to 71106 or 71108 on its face from the titles; their texts were not read. The medicaid.gov guidance page, read on 2026-11-03, lists guidance for section 71107 (letter of 2026-03-06 and slide deck posted 2026-04-03) and for other sections of the law (71109, 71115 to 71118, 71401), but none for sections 71103 to 71106 or 71108. The HHS press release of 2025-07-17 was read; later state results of the duplicate-enrollment rechecks were not found. Work requirements and cost sharing are covered in c14-05, whose proposal also includes more robust eligibility determinations, so this record overlaps c14-05 on that one item.
